hypotheses.justification: This follows from `hfB`. `JetPrototype.Phase` is `(Transverse × ℝ) × Velocity`, built from Euclidean spaces, so it has the element `0`. Then `0 ≤ |f 0| ≤ R`, i.e. `le_trans (abs_nonneg _) (hfB 0)`, gives `0 ≤ R`, and that term can be passed wherever the proof used `hR`. Downstream, `PositiveIntegral.along_time_bound` takes it only as the unused binder `_hR`. In this file `time_difference` only uses it to build the nonnegativity proof for `size_difference`, which can also be built from the derived fact.

This follows from `hg` in the same way: `0 ≤ |g 0| ≤ S` by `le_trans (abs_nonneg _) (hg 0)`, using `(0 : ℝ × JetPrototype.Phase)`. Replace each use of `hS` with that term. `along_time_bound` takes it only as the unused binder `_hS`, and elsewhere it is only used to prove `0 ≤ L*R+S`.

Split on the sign of `T`. If `0 ≤ T`, the existing proof works. If `T < 0`, then `PositiveIntegral.time T t = max 0 (min T t)` (definition in PositiveIntegralFixedPoint.lean). Since `min T t ≤ T < 0`, this equals `0` for every `t`. `PositiveIntegral.value T L flow f₀ g (t,p)` depends on `t` only through `time T t`, so `hf` gives `f (t,p) = value T L JetBarrier.flight f₀ g (0,p)` for all `t`. Hence `fun t => size (fun p => f (t,p))` is constant and `continuous_const` proves the claim. The other hypotheses are not needed in this case.
